{"criterion": "Maturities are laddered and covered, with covenant headroom disclosed but thin, or not disclosed.", "why": "(1) FACT [dm.ladder]: the notes-and-term-loan ladder is disclosed in full — "As of May 29, 2025, maturities of notes payable and the term loan by fiscal year were as follows:\nRemainder of 2025 | $—", "2026 | —\n2027 | —\n2028 | 600", "2029 | 2,384", "2030 and thereafter | 9,500", "Unamortized issuance costs, discounts, and premium, net | (50)\n$12,434". (2) INFERENCE [from 1]: no note or term-loan principal matures in fiscal 2025, 2026 or 2027; the first scheduled maturity is $600 million in fiscal 2028, and roughly three-quarters of the $12,434 million total falls in "2030 and thereafter". (3) FACT [dm.ladder]: the lease ladder is separately disclosed — "Remainder of 2025 | $150 | $23\n2026 | 674 | 91\n2027 | 652 | 94\n2028 | 630 | 87\n2029 | 536 | 82\n2030 and thereafter | 955 | 433\nLess imputed interest\n(490) | (138)\n$3,107 | $672". (4) FACT [dm.instrument, "Total debt"]: "$538 | $15,003 | $15,541 | $431 | $12,966 | $13,397" (current | long-term | total carrying value, May 29 2025 vs August 29 2024). (5) INFERENCE [from 3, 4]: the $538 million of current debt is the current portion of finance lease obligations, not a bullet maturity, since the notes/term-loan ladder shows nil due before fiscal 2028.

(6) FACT [filing body, accession 0000723125-25-000021]: "Cash and marketable investments totaled $12.21 billion as of May 29, 2025, and $9.15 billion as of August 29, 2024." (7) FACT [dm.revolver]: "As of May 29, 2025, $3.50 billion was available to draw under our Revolving Credit Facility." (8) FACT [dm.revolver]: "Any amounts outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility would mature on March 12, 2030 and amounts borrowed may be prepaid without penalty." (9) INFERENCE [from 1, 3, 6, 7, 8]: cash and investments alone exceed every scheduled principal and lease payment through fiscal 2029 as laid out in the two ladders, and the revolver's own expiry sits beyond the first two note maturities — so the near-dated obligations are covered without recourse to new financing.

(10) FACT [filing body]: "For the first nine months of 2025, net cash provided by financing activities consisted primarily of $1.68 billion of proceeds from the issuance of the 2029 Term Loan A; approximately $1.25 billion of proceeds from the issuance of the 2035 B Notes; approximately $1.00 billion of proceeds from the issuance of the 2035 A Notes; and $499 million of proceeds from the issuance of the 2032 Notes; partially offset by $3.60 billion of repayments of debt, which included the prepayment of the 2026 Notes, 2026 Term Loan A, 2027 Notes, and 2027 Term Loan A borrowings". (11) INFERENCE [from 10, 1]: the maturities that would have fallen inside the next three fiscal years were prepaid during the period rather than left to be refinanced, and the replacement paper was termed out to 2029–2035; this is refinancing already executed, not assumed.

(12) FACT [dm.covenant]: "The Term Loan Agreement requires us to maintain, on a consolidated basis, a net leverage ratio of total net indebtedness to adjusted EBITDA, as defined in the Term Loan Agreement and calculated as of the last day of each fiscal quarter, not to exceed 3.25 to 1.00, subject to a temporary four fiscal quarter increase in such maximum ratio to 3.75 to 1.00 following certain material acquisitions." (13) FACT [dm.covenant]: "The Revolving Credit Facility contains the same net leverage ratio and substantially the same other covenants as the Term Loan Agreement."

INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (covenant headroom)
  needed: the computed actual net leverage ratio at May 29, 2025, the adjusted-EBITDA denominator as defined in the Term Loan Agreement, or a statement of compliance.
  why: the bundle records dm.headroom as not_found — "the filing states the maximum ratio but discloses no computed actual ratio, no adjusted EBITDA figure, and no statement of compliance"; E-04 separately confirms adjusted EBITDA appears "only as a covenant term in the Term Loan Agreement discussion" with no reconciliation. I am barred from deriving it.
  would_change: if a disclosed ratio sat well inside 3.25x, the first rubric option would become available; if it sat at or above 3.25x, the "covenant headroom is exhausted or breached" option would.

(14) FACT [sc.diluted]: "Weighted-average common shares outstanding – Diluted | 1,125 | 1,123 | 1,123 | 1,104" — 1,125 million for the quarter ended May 29, 2025 against 1,123 million a year earlier, and 1,123 million for the nine months against 1,104 million. (15) FACT [ca.issuance, status not_found]: "Statements of Changes in Equity show only shares issued under equity compensation plans; no public or private equity offering disclosed." (16) FACT [ca.buyback]: "No shares were repurchased in the first nine months of 2025." (17) INFERENCE [from 14, 15, 16]: the share count rose, but every identified source of new shares is equity compensation, and the absence of buybacks — not an equity raise — is what left the count un-offset; nothing in the bundle shows stock issued to fund operations.

Downside arithmetic
(18) FACT [filing body, Consolidated Statements of Operations]: "Operating income (loss) | 2,169 | 719 | 6,116 | (218)" and "Net income (loss) | $1,885 | $332 | $5,338 | $(109)" — the nine months ended May 30, 2024 is the worst earnings period visible. (19) FACT [filing body]: "Interest expense | (123) | (150) | (353) | (426)". (20) FACT [filing body]: "Net cash provided by operating activities | 11,795 | 5,102" (nine months FY2025 and FY2024). (21) INFERENCE [from 18, 19, 20]: in the worst period the bundle contains, the company ran an operating loss and a net loss yet generated $5,102 million of operating cash against $426 million of nine-month interest expense — operating cash flow exceeded interest by a wide margin even in the trough shown. (22) FACT [filing body, risk factors]: "In the past five years, annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low-teen percentage range to a minus high-40% range." (23) INFERENCE [from 18, 22]: the bundle's worst visible period is a nine-month window inside a cycle the company itself describes as swinging far harder over five years, so it is a partial test, not a full-cycle one.

INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (leverage ratios, peer context, scenario figures)
  needed: gross and net debt/EBITDA for this and prior periods, period-aligned peer leverage, and any pre-computed downside scenario.
  why: the bundle contains no <computed_metrics> block, no peer set, and no EBITDA figure of any kind (E-04: no non-GAAP measure is presented). I will not derive them.
  would_change: if disclosed leverage were low and below peers, the evidence would push toward the top option provided headroom were also disclosed; if high, toward the breach option.

Contingent and off-balance-sheet items
(24) FACT [filing body]: a jury "found that Micron should pay $425 million for infringement of the '912 patent and $20 million for infringement of the '417 patent", and "Micron expects to appeal the verdict". (25) FACT [filing body]: "We are unable to predict the outcome of any of the matters noted above and cannot make a reasonable estimate of the potential loss or range of possible losses." (26) INFERENCE [from 24, 25]: no accrual amount for these matters is disclosed, so their balance-sheet effect is unquantified in the bundle; $445 million of adverse verdicts is small against $12.21 billion of cash and investments (fact 6) but the appeal outcome and other unquantified matters are not sized. (27) FACT [filing body]: "As of May 29, 2025, excluded obligations consisted of $1.02 billion of finance lease obligations over a weighted-average period of 14 years for gas supply arrangements deemed to contain embedded leases and equipment leases." (28) FACT [gd.value, PP&E purchase obligations]: "approximately $1.69 billion", "substantially all of which is expected to be paid within one year". (29) FACT [gd.value, capex FY2025]: "approximately $14 billion" net of government incentives. (30) INFERENCE [from 28, 29]: the largest calls on cash over the next year are discretionary capital spending and purchase commitments, not debt service — and the company states capex "will vary depending on market conditions" (gd.language_note), which is the lever available in a downturn. (31) FACT [filing body, AOCI table]: "Pension Liability Adjustments" of $38 million in accumulated other comprehensive income; the bundle contains no pension obligation, funded status or contribution schedule — a data gap.

(32) INFERENCE [from 2, 9, 11, 12, 13, and the headroom gap]: the ladder is disclosed and the near-dated obligations are covered, which rules out the two options resting on an undisclosed ladder or an assumed refinancing; the single fact that keeps this off the top option is that the tested ratio and threshold are disclosed while the actual ratio and headroom are not.", "what_would_move_it_down": "A disclosed note or term-loan principal maturity falling inside the next three fiscal years that the filing indicated would be met by refinancing rather than by cash on hand or a committed facility would move me to "A maturity falls inside the horizon and refinancing is assumed rather than committed.""}
